transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-12-18
Start: 14:00 PST
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Evan Carter (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Luis Ortega (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (Saffron - Head of ML), Ravi Shah (Saffron - Eng Manager), Hannah Lowe (Saffron - Product), Omar Diaz (Saffron - Security)

Summary: quick POC weekly sync to triage a regression spike after last prompt tweak, review evaluation metrics (precision/recall/hallucination rate), align on guardrail changes, and decide whether to freeze prompt-set-A or move forward with set-B for the next stage.

00:00 - 00:28 Evan Carter: hey everybody, thanks for joining, we'll do a quick check, uh, 30 minutes or so then Qs, we got the regression report you all sent, thanks for the dataset and extra logs
00:30 - 00:58 Maya Patel: thanks, yeah we saw a hop in hallucination rate after yesterday's prompt changes, up about 6 percentage points on the live eval, so wanted to go over root cause and options
01:05 - 01:40 Priya Nair: ok, cool. we pulled the eval harness and ran A/B - prompt-set-A (baseline) vs prompt-set-B (the tweak with extra context preface). set-B improved intent precision for classification but introduced more open-ended completions which look like hallucinations in the scoring rubric
01:45 - 02:20 Ravi Shah: just to be clear, our success criteria are 92% intent precision and <3% hallucination on the top-5 responses, right? Hannah, is that still accurate?
02:25 - 02:50 Hannah Lowe: yes that's what product agreed, and also latency threshold of 450ms p50 for inline chat flows — anything more impacts UX regressively
03:00 - 03:30 Luis Ortega: quick note — when we ran the local bench the p50 was 380ms on the hosted endpoint but the dedicated config with 2x batching went to 520ms p50 for long context due to KV cache cold starts
03:35 - 04:10 Omar Diaz: on security, we still need the network diagram + KMS integration guide from Redwood, plus clarification on log retention policies for the private deployment option
04:15 - 04:50 Evan Carter: we'll share the docs, link is in the deck we sent earlier (see: https://redwood.example/poc/saffron/infra-deck) — also, quick note: dedicated instances can be tuned w/ pre-warmed KV cache to reduce cold-start latency, that's a config we can demo
04:55 - 05:40 Maya Patel: back to the regression — Priya, can you walk through a couple of failure examples? we attached three in the spreadsheet but wanted your read on patterns
05:45 - 06:30 Priya Nair: sure, example one: prompt A generated a conservative summary, no fabricated entities. prompt B included the project brief preface and model invented a company name in the summary — scoring marked that as hallucination. we think the extra preface increased creative sampling when temperature wasn't lowered in the generation params
06:35 - 07:10 Ravi Shah: ah ok so it's mixing prompt engineering effect + sampling defaults. did you adjust temperature or top_p between runs?
07:15 - 07:45 Priya Nair: between A/B we left sampling same to isolate prompt impact. next step could be either tune decoding params (temp 0.0-0.2) or lock guardrails — like system-level instruction blocking certain tokens/entities
07:50 - 08:25 Evan Carter: another lever is constrained decoding + entity whitelist from your CRM - that reduces hallucinations for facts like company names but can be brittle if the set is large
08:30 - 09:10 Hannah Lowe: what about reranking? we noticed the top-1 answer often had highest fluency but lower factuality score. can we add an embeddings-based reranker to the pipeline?
09:15 - 09:55 Priya Nair: yes, we prototyped a re-ranker using similarity to golden responses and a factuality classifier. It shaved the hallucination rate by ~2.4 points on the benchmark, but added ~60-80ms to tail latency; tradeoff depends on SLOs
10:00 - 10:40 Maya Patel: for the customer-facing flow we can't exceed 550ms p95. If reranker pushes us past that we need to consider dedicated capacity or partial reranking (only for low-confidence cases)
10:45 - 11:20 Luis Ortega: we also saw that quantized model variant reduced latency but increased hallucination in edge cases — likely due to reduced numeric precision on attention softmax, odd but reproducible on small samples
11:25 - 12:00 Ravi Shah: okay, so options on table: revert to prompt-set-A baseline, or adopt prompt-set-B plus tuning: lowered temperature + reranking on low-confidence outputs + entity whitelist. Which path reduces manual maintenance?
12:05 - 12:50 Priya Nair: prompt-set-A is stable but doesn't reach the new intent precision goal. set-B with adjustments hits precision target in most slices but needs engineering around rerank/whitelist. For maintainability, hybrid approach: freeze golden prompts for critical intents, allow free-form for exploratory prompts with stricter guardrails
12:55 - 13:40 Evan Carter: thinking about pilot timeline — if we lock a hybrid policy now, we can run a 2-week focused dedicated pilot (approx numbers in pricing) to validate at scale. I'll send pricing. Also mention: burst capacity policy for Black Friday-like spikes — optional add-on
13:45 - 14:20 Hannah Lowe: can Redwood run a stress test with synthetic traffic that simulates our 95th percentile session length? we want to see KV cache warm-up behavior under realistic patterns
14:25 - 15:10 Priya Nair: yes, we can run a synthetic replay harness. we'll include trace-level metrics and token-level breakdowns so you can see where batching interacts with latency and cost. we'll also capture failure cases for the regression suite
15:15 - 15:55 Omar Diaz: security - please include SSO flows in the replay if possible and confirm logs do not contain PII by default. also need the timeline for SOC 2 docs we asked for
16:00 - 16:35 Evan Carter: we'll provide SOC 2 artifact bundle and the SSO/SAML integration guide. KMS spec too. link: [security-pack.zip] (we'll email).
16:40 - 17:20 Maya Patel: about metrics in the regression report — we want confusion matrices by intent, hallucination examples bucketed by hallucination type, and a precision/recall curve for the top-10 intents. can Redwood produce those or do we share labels?
17:25 - 18:00 Priya Nair: we can generate the confusion matrices if you supply the labeled gold set; we can also surface failure cases and categorize them heuristically and you can validate. our evaluation harness accepts CSV with columns: prompt,response,gold_intent,confidence
18:05 - 18:45 Ravi Shah: quick Q on pricing — if we move to dedicated for 2 weeks, are there pro-rated discounts? Evan?
18:50 - 19:25 Evan Carter: yes, pro-rated monthly reserved capacity applies, and we can include a short-term burst policy to cover spikes. I'll layout numbers in the quote and include cost delta for reranker latency overhead
19:30 - 20:10 Hannah Lowe: loop back to guardrails — can Redwood enforce a deny-list and a token-level post-check? We had a previous vendor who did post-filtering but it was slow
20:15 - 21:00 Priya Nair: we support efficient post-checks using token-level rules and a lightweight classifier. post-filtering is cheap if you run it only on top candidate or on low-confidence bins; doing it on all beams is expensive
21:05 - 21:45 Luis Ortega: FYI we saw a YAML config bug yesterday that flipped a shuffle param in the prompt pipeline, that likely contributed to a subset of the regressions. engineering patched it but it's a reminder to pin infra configs in the harness
21:50 - 22:30 Maya Patel: oh that explains a few of the weird cases - thanks for catching. so is the plan: Priya runs full regression on set-B, we review failure cases, decide freeze/hybrid, and Evan sends pricing + docs?
22:35 - 23:10 Evan Carter: yep that's the plan. I'll also propose dates for a dedicated pilot kickoff if you opt in. we'll include a checklist: SSO test, KMS handshake, golden prompt freeze, and stress test scope
23:15 - 23:55 Hannah Lowe: can we get the next sync scheduled for Tues 2025-12-23 to decide? that's tight but aligns w/ our holiday push
24:00 - 24:20 Evan Carter: Tuesday works for us, we'll tentatively schedule and confirm by email

Meeting close: recap of decisions and concrete next steps. Links shared: deck (https://redwood.example/poc/saffron/infra-deck), regression report (uploaded to shared drive), security-pack (to be emailed).

Notes on transcription: occasional mislabels and run-on lines; some technical terms spelled phonetically (e.g., 'KV cache' sometimes transcribed as 'k v cache') — treat with usual caution.

End of transcript.
